full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquce J. In the aforesaid two Criminal Miscellaneous Cases, the High Court Division observed that the time limit as provided in 20Ka of the Durnity Daman Commission Ain, 2004 (the Act) is mandatory in nature, thereby, it quashed the proceedings. Against which, these two criminal petitions have been filed by the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC). Since the points determination of these two petitions are the same, they are being disposed of by this common judgment. 

 2. Respondent No.1 of Criminal Miscellaneous Petition No.759 of 2019 filed an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure in the High Court Division for quashing the proceeding of Special. Case No.05 of 2018 arising out of Dudak GR. Case No.171 of 2015 corresponding to Ukhia Police Station Case No.19 dated 12.05.2015 under sections 409,420,109 of Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, pending trial in the Court of Divisional Special judge, Special Tribunal No.1, Cox's Bazar. The High Court Division issued Rule, which was registered as Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.32933 of 2018. Finally, the High Court Division, by the impugned judgment and order dated 09.12.2018, made the Rule absolute and thereby, quashed the afore-said proceeding. 

 3. Respondent No.1 of Criminal Miscellaneous Petition No.760 of 2019 filed an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure in the High Court Division for quashing the proceeding of Special Case No.03 of 2018 arising out of Dudak G.R. Case No.167 of 2015 corresponding to Ukhia Police Station Case No.15 dated. 12.05.2015 under sections 409,420,109 of Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, pending trial in the Court of Division Special Judge, Special Tribunal .No.1, Cox's Bazar. The High Court Division issued Rule, which was registered as Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.32934 of 2018. Finally, the High Court Division, by the impugned judgment and order dated 09.12.2018, made the Rule absolute and thereby, quashed the aforesaid proceeding. 

 4. The High Court Division quashed both the proceedings mainly on the ground that since the Investigating. Officer failed to complete investigation of the cases within the period as stipulated in 20Ka(1) and 20Ka(2) of the Act, continuation of those proceedings were bad in law. 

 5. Mr. Mohammad Shafiullah, Deputy Assistant Director, Combined District Office, Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC), Chittagong-2 as informant lodged the instant First Information Report (FIR) against the accused-respondent along with three others in Ukhiya Police Station Case No.19 dated 12.05.2015 under sections 409,420,109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act; 1947 alleging, interalia, that a prima facie case of corruption ,was discovered during an Investigation under E/R Nos.35/2014 and 46/2014. During the financial years 2013-2014 taka 2,40,64,000/- (two crore forty lac and sixty-four thousand taka only) was sanctioned under a program, namely, “অতি দরিদ্রদের জন্য কর্মসংস্থান কর্মসূচী, ২য় পর্যায়”, for 3,008 beneficiaries of. Ukhiya Upazila. By this allotment, according to the decision of Ukhiya Upazila Parisad, 6(six) projects have been approved for 450 beneficiaries of Palang. Khali Union, among those for the project of “জামতলী বাঘঘোনা রাজাইক্কা কাঠের ব্রীজ হতে মোছারখোলা স্কুল পযন্ত রাস্তার উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প" taka 6,00,000/- (six lac) was sanctioned for 75 beneficiaries. According to the policy of “অতি দরিদ্রদের জন্য কর্মসংস্থান কর্মসূচী" selected workers are entitled to get taka 200 (two hundred) for 35 cubic feet soil work, 5 (five) days a week. According to the policy, the Upazila Nirbahi Officer appointed Ashoke Kumer Achayarjo, Instructor, Ukhia Upazila Resource Centre, Ukhiya as Tag Officer by his office Memo No. 51.01.2294.03.96.2013-2014/108 dated 30.04.2013. Different project committees were created with different per-sons holding posts in the Union Parishad and other interested persons were approved by the Upazila Project Implementation Officer (accused-respondent) and Upazila Nirbahi Officer. Without carrying out any work and with-out informing others Project Chairman, Abdus Sukur, Tag Officer, Ashuk Kumer Achayerjo and Field Supervisor, Md. Jamal Hossain and Project Implementation Officer, Shafiqul Alam withdrew total taka 5,91,600.00 (five lac ninety one thousand and six hundred taka) from Sonali Bank, Ukhiya Branch in eight installments showing false signatures of 75 workers which was proved by analyzing records and paper documents and as such, they misappropriated the entire money and thus, the accused-respondent and 03 (three) others commit-ted offences and hence the case. 

 6. Mr. Mohammad Shafiullah, Deputy Assistant Director, Combined District Office, Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC), Chittagong-2 as informant lodged the instant First Information Report (FIR) against the accused-respondent along with three others in Ukhiya Police Station Case No. 15 dated 12.05.2015 under sections 409, 420, 109 of the Penal Code read with under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 alleging, inter-alia, that a prima facie case of corruption was discovered during an inquiry under E/R Nos.35/2014 and 46/2014. During the financial years 2013-2014 taka 1,85,92,000.00 (one crore eightyfive lac and ninety-two thousand) was sanctioned under a program, namely, “অতি দরিদ্রদের জন্য কর্মসংস্থান কর্মসূচী, ২য় পর্যায় for 2,656 beneficiaries of Ukhiya Upazila. By this allotment, according to the decision of Ukhiya Upazila Parisad, 9(nine) projects have been approved for 381 beneficiaries of Palang Khali Union, among those for the project of “বালূখালি উচ্চ বিদ্যালয়ের ফুটবল খেলার মাঠ সংস্কার ও বালূখালি ছড়া পুনঃখনন প্রকল্প” taka 14,42,000/- (fourteen lac and forty-two thousand) was sanctioned for 206 beneficiaries. According to the policy of “অতি দরিদ্রদের জন্য কর্মসংস্থান কর্মসূচী, selected workers are entitled to get taka 175(one hundred and seventy-five) for 35 cubic feet of soil work, 05 (five) days a week. That according to the policy, the Upazila Nirbahi Officer appointed Abdul Karim, Coordinator, ১টি বাড়ী ১টি খামার প্রকল্প, উখিয়া Instructor, Upazila Resource Centre, Ukhiya as Tag Officer by his office Memo No.51.01.2294.03.96.2012- 2013/241 dated 31.03.2013. Different project committees were created with different persons holding posts in the Union Parishad and other interested persons were approved by the Upazila Project Implementation Officer (accused-respondent) and Upazila Nirbahi Officer. Without carrying out any work and with-out informing others Project Chairman-Fozol Kader Bhutto, Tag Officer-Mohammad Abdul Karim, Field Supervisor- Md. Jamal Hossain and Project Implementation Officer Shafiqul Alam withdrew total taka 14,37,625.00 (fourteen lac thirty-seven thousand and six hundred twenty-five) from Sonali Bank, Ukhiya Branch in eight installments showing false 206 workers which was proved by analyzing records and documents and as such, they misappropriated the entire money and thus, the accused-respondent and 03 (three) others committed offences and hence the case. 

 7. The High Court Division quashed both the proceedings mainly on the ground that since the investigating officer failed to complete investigation of the cases within the period as stipulated in 20Ka(1) and 20Ka(2) of the Act, continuation of those proceedings were bad in law. 

 8. Mr. M. A. Aziz Khan, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the Anti-Corruption Commission in both the petitions, submits that the time stipulated for completion of investigation provided in section 20Ka of the Act is directory in nature, the High Court Division committed an error of law in treating the time limit for completion of investigation as mandatory provision, thereby, held that since Investigating Officer failed to investigate the respective cases within the stipulated time, the proceedings should be quashed and such wrong interpretation has caused a total failure of justice. 

 9. Mr. Golam Ahmed, learned Advocate for respondent No.1 in Criminal Miscellaneous Petition Nos. 32933 of 2018 and 32934 of 2018, in his submission supported the judgment and order of the High Court Division. He also adds that on a plain reading it is clear that this provision is mandatory and not a directory. It appears from record that the Investigation Officer, Mr. Mohammad Safiullah, Deputy Assistant Director, Combined District Office, Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC), Chittagong-2 took charge of investigation of the instant case on 22.09.2015 and submitted charge sheet after investigation on 21.07.2016 and that this time is beyond the longtime of statutory time limit for investigation. He further adds that the Investigations Officer was in no way authorized to do this in violation of the mandatory provision of section 20A of the Act and as such, we cannot legally approve this unlawful investigation, which has been conducted beyond the scope of law. Lastly, he submits that continuation of those proceedings on the basis of an unlawful investigation is an abuse of the process of the Court and accordingly, the proceeding of the case is liable to be quashed. 

 12. On perusal of the record, it appears that the First Information Report (FIR) was lodged by one Mr. Mohammad Safiullah, Deputy Assistant Director, Combined District Office, Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) Chittagong-2 and he took charge of investigation of the instant two cases on 22.09.2015 and according to section 20.A of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, his stipulated time for investigation including extended time (i.e., 180 working days) expired on 12.06.2016. It also appears that section 20A of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 has been inserted by section 8 of the Anti-Corruption Commission (Amendment) Act, 2013 (Act No. 60 of 2013) and this new section 20A runs as follows: 

 (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), if the investigation cannot be completed within the specified period on any reason-able grounds, the Investigating Officer may apply for extension of time to the Commission and in such case, the Commission may extend the period of time not exceeding 60 (sixty) working days. 

 (3) If the Investigating Officer fails to complete the investigation within the specified period mentioned in subsection (1) or, as the case may be, in sub-section (2) - 

 (b) the relevant officer shall be subjected to departmental proceeding on an accusation of inefficiency in accordance with laws or rules-regulations applicable to the Commission, police or the relevant organization, as the case may bed" 

 13. The learned Judges of the Division Bench of the High Court Division hold the view that on a plain reading it is clear that this provision is mandatory and not directory and it appears from the record that the Investigating Officer, Mr. Mohammad Safiullah, Deputy Assistant Director, Combined District Office, Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC), Chittagong-2 took charge of investigation of the instant case on 02.11.2015 and submitted charge sheet after investigation on 30.01.2018 and that this time is beyond the longtime of statutory time limit for investigation. It has been further held that the Investigating Officer was in no way authorized to do this in violation of the mandatory provision of section 20A of the Act and as such, we cannot legally approve this unlawful investigation, which has been conducted beyond the scope of the law. It has been also held that continuation of the proceeding of the case against the petitioner on the basis of an unlawful investigation is an abuse of the process of the Court and accordingly, the proceeding of the case is liable to be quashed. 

 14. On perusal of the above provision of law, we find that the Investigating Officer is lawfully obliged to submit charge-sheet within 180 working days from the date of receipt of the letter empowering him to investigate the matter. It is true that the Investigating Officer submitted charge-sheet before the concerned Court on 24.07.2016 having received a sanction. In this respect, the Durnity Daman Commission relied upon the case of Anti-Corruption Commission Vs. AAM Habibur Rahman reported in 67 DLR (AD) 278 in which it has been held by the Appellate Division that the provision of completion of within the stipulated period is not mandatory in nature and as such, non-submission of the report by the Investigating Agency within the stipulated working days cannot be a ground for quashing the proceedings since no consequences have been approved in law regarding the proceedings. Under the circumstances, it cannot be said that the time-frame for investigation is mandatory rather it can, at the best, be treated as directory.  16. Having considered those fact circumstances and other materials on record, we are inclined to hold that under no circumstances the proceedings of Special Tribunal Case No.03 of 2018 arising out of Ukhiya Police Station Case No.15 dated 12.05.2015 corresponding to G.R No.167 of 2015 under sections 409,420,109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and another one Special Case No.05 of 2018 arising out of Dudok G.R Case No.171 of 2015 corresponding under sections 409,420,109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act,1947 now pending in the Court of Special Tribunal No.1, Cox's Bazar liable to be quashed. 

 18. Hence, the impugned judgments and orders passed in Special Tribunal Case No.03 of 2018 arising out of Dudak G.R. Case No.167 of 2015 corresponding to Ukhiya Police Station Case No.15 dated 12.05.2015 under sections 409,420,1.09 of Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, pending trial in the Court of Divisional Special Judge, in Special Tribunal No.1, Cox's Bazar and another one Special. Case No.05 of 2018 arising out of Dudak G.R Case No.171 of 2015 corresponding to Ukhiya Police Station Case No.19 dated 12.05.2015 under sections 409,420,109 of Penal Code red with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 pending trial in the Court of Divisional Special Judge, in Special Tribunal No.1, Cox's Bazar are hereby set-aside.
